project.name: Modality Flow
project.status: daily mobility coach with fused map journey and Pass Flow ticketing

productVision.goal: Create a daily mobility habit: open app, see recommendation, use the intelligent map, start Pass Flow, finish trip, earn XP.
productVision.targetExperience: Coach-like home screen with a large recommendation card, current hour, simple weather/traffic context, tracked city Montpellier, XP, streak and badge progression.

frontend.webFix: index.ts uses registerRootComponent(App) so Expo Web mounts into #root

ai.note: Current model is a deterministic production-shaped simulation, ready to replace with RandomForest/XGBoost artifact.

home.purpose: Daily coach. Shows what to choose now, not raw KPIs.
home.decisionExample: If weather is stable, air is acceptable, traffic is high and bikes are available, bike is recommended and car is penalized.

map.purpose: Main app surface. Fuses map, journey calculation, station choice and Pass Flow.
map.note: Native mobile version is Mapbox-ready. Web version now uses real OpenStreetMap raster tiles with API markers overlaid; no fake street canvas remains.

journey.purpose: Legacy screen kept in code but removed from final navigation. Journey is now handled on the map.
journey.logic: Uses effective location: real Montpellier position if inside city, otherwise follows Montpellier from Comedie. Sends temperature, precipitation, wind, AQI, trafficIndex and hour to backend.

features: device token UUID persisted in AsyncStorage
real qr_data display when returned by API
refund recovery with terminal_id query param

stations.GET /stations: All stations with health and availability ratio.

journey.POST /journey: Computes multimodal route options and ranks them by AI score.
journey.railway: Mobile calls the official Railway /journey endpoint directly.

prediction.POST /stations/{station_id}/predict: Predicts bike availability for a station.

ticketing.GET /remboursement/{ticket_id}/recuperer: Refund recovery. terminal_id is query parameter.

tam.GET /tam/stops: Official Railway /tam/stops returning GTFS TAM stops.
tam.GET /tam/routes: Official Railway /tam/routes returning GTFS TAM routes.

knownDesignDecisions.mapbox: Native mobile keeps rnmapbox. Web uses MapScreen.web.tsx fallback because rnmapbox web caused missing mapbox-gl CSS dependency.
knownDesignDecisions.icons: Custom text-based Icon component replaces @expo/vector-icons on web to avoid Expo SDK 51 expo-font incompatibility.
knownDesignDecisions.expoWeb: apps/mobile/index.ts registers App with registerRootComponent. This fixed the previous blank page where #root had zero children.
knownDesignDecisions.environmentData: Currently simulated city signals. Can later be replaced by Open-Meteo, Atmo, TAM, GBFS and real traffic providers.
knownDesignDecisions.trackedCityMode: If the real GPS location is outside Montpellier, the app shows approximate access time to Montpellier and continues with Montpellier as the followed city.
knownDesignDecisions.endpointProtection: apps/mobile/src/services/api.ts blocks any request path starting with /lille. Backend ticket proxy also blocks forbidden prefixes.
knownDesignDecisions.deviceToken: Generated once with crypto randomUUID/getRandomValues fallback and stored in AsyncStorage. No hardcoded device token.
knownDesignDecisions.qrPolicy: PassCard displays qr_data returned by API. If missing, it says QR indisponible pour ce trajet.

verification.apiBuild: npm.cmd run build in apps/api passed
verification.docker: docker compose up -d --build ran successfully earlier

startupRoadmap: Replace simulated environment signals with real Open-Meteo, Atmo, TAM/GTFS and GBFS integrations.
Add push notifications for empty stations, high pollution and better alternatives.
Add production observability, rate limiting and Redis cache for realtime provider data.
Train station-level RandomForest/XGBoost models from historical data.
Build B2B SaaS dashboard for cities, campuses and operators.
questionsForReviewer: Does the current app satisfy the objective of a user-friendly recommendation based on hour, weather, AQI and traffic?
Which endpoints should be connected to real external data first?
Is the journey scoring formula product-ready or should weights be adjusted?
What is missing to make this investor-ready?
